blocking.section: Decision outcome (HTTP/3 row) and Decision drivers
blocking.issue: The HTTP/3 path has no resource bounds. The drivers promise per-connection stream, buffer and frame limits 'as the data plane's Bounded resources table fixes them', but every ceiling in the ADR and in that table is an HTTP2Config or net.Listener mechanism, and none of them reaches quic-go. The Node connection ceiling is 'a counting net.Listener [that] stops calling Accept', which cannot count QUIC connections on a UDP socket. quic-go's incoming-stream count and connection and stream flow-control windows are quic.Config settings; to my knowledge they default to 100 streams and receive windows that auto-tune into megabytes. quic-go's http3.Server also keeps its own header limit, separate from the 256 KiB Server.MaxHeaderBytes. On top of that, no research shows that quic-go's ResponseWriter honors http.ResponseController read and write deadlines, and the Deadlines row and the data plane's retirement protocol depend on them. As written, one HTTP/3 connection can hold far more than the 592 KiB (hypothesis) the data plane budgets per connection, and the roughly 19 GiB worst-case Node sum does not hold. That contradicts System overview's 'Bounded everything' principle.
blocking.evidence: "**Bounded resources**: per-connection stream, buffer and frame limits and per-request deadlines, as the data plane's [Bounded resources](../architecture/03-data-plane.md#bounded-resources) table fixes them." and "| HTTP/3 | quic-go `http3` v0.63.x, pinned, on UDP at the `https` listener's port when `http3: true`, with the same Routes, Policies and certificates, behind an internal interface; a build constraint keeps it out of FIPS builds (OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9) | Planned (M3) |"; data plane: "Client connections per Node | 20,000 connections (target); a counting `net.Listener` stops calling `Accept` at the ceiling"
blocking.fix: Extend the HTTP/3 row: 'QUIC connections count against the Node connection ceiling, and quic-go's incoming-stream, receive-window and header limits are set no higher than the HTTP/2 ceilings, with request deadlines through http.ResponseController; the quic-go field names and deadline support await research (proposed Data plane Bounded resources rows)'. Add the matching item to the 'Proposed owning-document amendments' bullet in More information. Add a Confirmation item: an HTTP/3 case in the Planned (M3) protocol suite that asserts the stream cap and per-connection memory against the data plane budget. The document is at about 1,494 of 1,500 words, so offset the additions by tightening, for example the v0.62.0 priorities bullet under 'net/http plus quic-go'.

blocking.section: Confirmation (FIPS job) and Decision outcome (HTTP/3 row)
blocking.issue: What a FIPS Node does with `http3: true` is left undecided ('refused or inert'), so the test cannot be written. The 'inert' branch also contradicts foundation pack section 8.1: a FIPS Node and a default Node would accept the same digest and behave differently, one serving UDP 8443 and the other not. The build constraint is not named either, so the FIPS job cannot pass it to `go list -deps` to prove that quic-go is absent.
blocking.evidence: "**FIPS job**, Planned (M5): fails if quic-go appears in the FIPS `ruralzd` dependencies ([ADR-0001](0001-implementation-language-go.md)), and FIPS tests assert that `http3: true` is refused or inert."; pack 8.1: "Equal digests mean equal effective behavior on every Node that accepts them"
blocking.fix: Decide 'refused'. A FIPS `ruralzd` rejects a Revision whose `https` listener sets `http3: true`: a deterministic NACK in Control mode and a load failure in file mode, with an RZ-CFG code that the Configuration model registers (listed as a proposed amendment, tied to OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9). Change the Confirmation to 'FIPS tests assert that a Revision with `http3: true` is rejected with that code'. Name the Ruralz build tag that the FIPS release target sets and that the HTTP/3 package excludes, so the FIPS job runs `go list -deps` with that tag.

blocking.issue: The row does not say whether HTTP2Config.StrictMaxConcurrentRequests is true or false, and 'honoring server limits' implies true. The research defines the field as 'whether to open a new connection when an existing one hits its stream limit'. If it is true, an Endpoint gets no second connection. Every request beyond the server's advertised stream limit (often 100 to 250) waits inside http.Transport, a queue that Ruralz's `circuitBreaker.maxPendingRequests`, the breaker and the in-flight accounting never see. Long-lived SSE or other streamed responses on that connection then starve short requests. If it is false, the 'honoring server limits' claim is wrong. Either way the upstream concurrency bound is hidden or unstated.
blocking.evidence: "| Upstream layer | Its own loop on `http.Transport`, not `httputil.ReverseProxy`; `http` Upstreams use HTTP/1.1 in cleartext and HTTP/2 by ALPN over TLS, honoring server limits through `HTTP2Config.StrictMaxConcurrentRequests` ([source](https://go.dev/doc/go1.26)) | Planned (M1) |"
blocking.fix: State the value and the bound, for example: 'StrictMaxConcurrentRequests false, with `http.Transport.MaxConnsPerHost` from `circuitBreaker.maxConnections`. Each attempt takes a per-Endpoint slot in Ruralz before RoundTrip, so no request waits inside http.Transport and waiters count toward `maxPendingRequests`.' If true is kept, state the per-Endpoint concurrency cap and how waiters count toward `maxPendingRequests`. Record the choice as a proposed Data plane Upstream layer amendment in More information, since the owning document carries the same sentence.

blocking.issue: The 'because' clause claims that every protocol library in foundation pack section 7 composes with net/http handlers. Most section 7 protocol libraries are clients or brokers with no net/http handler: franz-go, nats.go/jetstream, paho.golang, mochi-mqtt, the grpc-go upstream client and rueidis. The decision rationale is therefore factually wrong as written, and coder/websocket, which does compose, is not in section 7 at all.
blocking.evidence: "Chosen option: \"`net/http` for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and h2c, plus quic-go for HTTP/3\", because every protocol library in foundation pack section 7 composes with `net/http` handlers,"
blocking.fix: Narrow the claim to the ingress libraries: 'because the ingress libraries, connect-go (foundation pack section 7), coder/websocket and SSE flushing through http.ResponseController (Tech stack), compose with net/http handlers'. This costs about the same number of words.

non_blocking.suggestion: Name the P1 tension. Foundation pack section 1 and P1 say the FIPS build has 'the same features', yet HTTP/3 is off in FIPS builds (pack 8.4). Add 'Bad, because FIPS builds lack HTTP/3, a feature difference P1 forbids until OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9 closes'.

'Only `HTTP2Config` fields (MaxConcurrentStreams, ...)' reads as an exhaustive list, yet other rows use HTTP2Config pings and StrictMaxConcurrentRequests. Write 'Only `HTTP2Config` fields, on client listeners MaxConcurrentStreams, ...'.

The ADR notes that floor (Go 1.26) and release (go1.27.1) builds run different HTTP/2 code, and Go 1.27 adds header-value limits and client priority. Say that the protocol conformance suite runs in both the floor and the release jobs, as the tech stack already requires for JSON golden tests.

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (HTTP/2 settings row) and Hot Reload
non_blocking.suggestion: Replacing the UDP socket when a listener changes, or when http3 is toggled by Hot Reload, loses in-flight QUIC connections the same way a binary upgrade does, because SO_REUSEPORT hashes packets across sockets. Mention it next to the ADR-0015 consequence, or route it to OQ-system-overview-18.
State that 0-RTT stays off, the quic-go default, or route it to an Open question: 0-RTT early data is replayable and would bypass the replay rule for non-idempotent Routes.

The dashed path from quic-go through the shared handler to coder/websocket and connect-go suggests that WebSocket and native gRPC work over HTTP/3. Multi-protocol says 'native gRPC and WebSocket need TCP' and that Extended CONNECT is Not planned. Add that to the caption or label the edge.
Use one name for the chosen option throughout: the Considered options item, the 'Chosen option' string and the Pros and cons H3 'net/http plus quic-go' use three different wordings.
The HTTP/3 discovery (Alt-Svc) gap is currently only a SHOULD for Data plane. Browsers never use UDP 8443 without discovery, so say that the M3 HTTP/3 row depends on it.
